claim: A q-query black-box auditor on a layer of M inputs cannot certify a universal trace property against semantics-preserving one-input trace mutations; some mutation is detected with probability at most q/M.

quantifiers.tester: every deterministic or randomized adaptive black-box tester with at most q queries
quantifiers.reference_program: every total deterministic reference program satisfying the surgical-wrapper hypothesis
quantifiers.counterexample: there exists a finite hidden input y and a total semantics-equivalent hard-coded-needle program P_y
quantifiers.scope_exclusion: no claim about white-box proof systems or proved finite fault domains

same_realization: declared observations returned on those inputs

experiment.chunking: not needed; one invocation completed below 30 seconds

barrier_audit.relativization: negative theorem relativizes to symmetric fixed oracles
barrier_audit.algebrization: algebraic trace encodings do not reveal an unqueried point
barrier_audit.natural_proofs: not the active framework; no circuit largeness/usefulness property is constructed
barrier_audit.missing_arrow: a solver-independent complete fault-domain or density theorem, or an all-program sound complete white-box proof system, with encoding normalization and all costs
